messages.author: d5fdb09d679f8c32
messages.subject: Re: AIC from fitqtl
parts:
Whether it would be appropriate is unclear, but you can always
calculate the AIC from the result of fitqtl.

Basically, if the LOD score corresponding to a model fittedd by fitqtl
is L, then AIC will be
-2*log(10)*L + 2*df,
where df is the degrees of freedom of the model.

In the context of QTL problems, Karl's investigations have shown that
a BIC-type penalty might be better.

I'll let Karl elaborate.

Saunak

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: AIC from fitqtl
parts:
The fitqtl function provides a log likelihood for a model (or, with
the drop-one-term analysis,
for a set of models). One can obtain AIC values from that by
subtracting the appropriate
penalty.

However, there's no reason to prefer the particular penalty in AIC;
it is derived by an asymptotic
argument and may not be behaved appropriately in regular-sized
samples. We are working on extending
our previous work on additive QTL models to the case that
interactions are to be considered, but
we're not quite there yet, and so I don't yet have advice concerning
criteria for comparing models.

karl
